static_traits.name: Chen Jing
static_traits.social_status: Due to avoiding swimsuit-related social activities, friendships are affected and social interaction is limited
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly organized; able to describe automatic thoughts and emotions; acknowledging many judgments are based on 'feelings rather than evidence'; overall negative tone but willing to explore alternative perspectives and small steps; good counseling cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I am afraid to wear a swimsuit because I believe others will mock me, seeing me as a worthless, overweight failure.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this fear significantly limits my social activities and self-expression.
growth_experiences: This fear began in adolescence, triggered by negative body image and worry about being evaluated; stress was initially very high, then persisted and worsened into adulthood, gradually developing into avoiding swimsuit-related occasions, affecting social life and self-confidence.

core_beliefs: I am a fat and completely worthless person

special_situations.event: When summer arrives or invited to pool parties/beach activities requiring swimsuits
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I wear a swimsuit, others will stare at my body and mock me; being mocked proves I have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids all occasions requiring wearing a swimsuit, reduces contact with friends to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone will laugh at me, thinking I am a worthless fat failure

special_situations.event: Before going out, thinks about possibly needing to wear a swimsuit or be photographed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose my body flaws, I will definitely embarrass myself next, be talked about, and humiliated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Imagining the worst outcome in advance, simply not going, to reduce current anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will definitely talk about me and laugh at me; I will be very embarrassed

special_situations.event: Sees one's body when looking in the mirror or trying on a swimsuit
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my appearance is not 'perfect' enough, it means I am an overall failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging appearance by extreme standards, negating other strengths, further avoiding socializing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I look terrible; this again proves I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Ordinary gazes or conversations of others in public places
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others glance at me or speak in low voices, they must be mocking me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing attention on others' reactions, constantly proving to oneself being belittled, thus quickly leaving the situation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Their looks and whispers are mocking me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and respected in presenting her true self and body
core_conflict.fear: Fears being mocked, humiliated, and rejected after exposing oneself
defense_goal: Reducing shame and anxiety by avoiding exposing the body and related occasions
Keeps distance from potential judges to maintain a sense of safety and self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: A shameful, vulnerable self easily mocked
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh others/groups with mocking and scrutinizing gazes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to examine evidence, challenge negative beliefs, or try new perspectives
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing change is 'unrealistic', insisting others will definitely judge them
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'avoidance is less hassle' in a tactful but firm tone, using 'this is unrealistic for me' to downplay the need to try changing.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing others' looks or social situations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Externally attributing inner self-derogation experiences as 'others look down on me and mock me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Asserting others' negative evaluations with declarative sentences, e.g. 'I can tell from their eyes', in a certain tone, hard to persuade.

manifestations: Avoids swimsuit-related activities for fear of being judged, gradually growing distant from friends
Never disclosing true distress to friends, experiencing inner isolation and estrangement
Fear and shame limit summer leisure and social choices
Repeatedly choosing avoidance to avoid anxiety, personal action space self-limited
outcomes: Lowered sense of control over own choices and life

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: In the narration, repeatedly uses 'they will laugh at me' and 'I can tell from their eyes' as the basis for judging others' negative evaluations
Externalizes inner shame and self-deprecation experiences as others' ridicule and contempt

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Turning the desire to socialize into self-limitation and withdrawal, choosing not to go on the grounds of 'less stress'
Never disclosing true distress to friends for a long time, instead bearing anxiety and shame alone

positive_force: Has several friends to talk with; potential support resources exist
Willing to explore alternative perspectives in counseling, able to identify negative thought patterns
Willing to try small-scale, low-risk exposure (such as with a few close friends)
Able to distinguish 'feelings' from 'evidence' in conversation, with some self-reflection ability
negative_force: Stable self-disparagement and low sense of self-worth
Marked cognitive distortions like mind reading, predicting the future, overgeneralization, and personalization
Uses avoidance as the main coping strategy: short-term anxiety reduction but long-term maintenance of fear
High negative attention to body image, strong shame

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids all social and leisure activities requiring a swimsuit
antecedent: When summer arrives or one is invited to a pool party / beach activity
Looking in the mirror or trying on a swimsuit, thinking of possibly being photographed
Negative automatic thoughts about body shape appearing
target_behavior.core_reason: Intense shame and self-deprecation about body image, accompanied by catastrophizing beliefs of mind reading and predicting the future (believing one will definitely be mocked and humiliated)
target_behavior.function: Escaping judgmental situations to quickly reduce anxiety and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Restricted social activities, damaged relationships with friends; decreased confidence and restricted self-expression, negative beliefs further reinforced
